what: gemma-4-31B decode rate on one A100 80G across attention backend x speculation x context depth. The forced TRITON_ATTN default loses 61% to MTP at 50K context; routing the same model to FlashInfer removes the collapse. CUDA-side control for the ROCm mechanism in docs/speculative-decoding-on-rdna.md and the measured basis for our comments on vllm#52049, vllm#47547 and vllm#50891.
why_it_is_here: The repository's speculative-decoding chapter claims the MTP collapse is a property of the Triton unified-attention kernel's 3D-to-2D drop, not of RDNA. That claim predicts the same collapse on any CUDA machine that routes gemma-4 onto the same kernel, deepening with context, and predicts its disappearance on a backend without the guard. Both predictions are what this matrix tests, and both held.
measured: 2026-08-26, two Colab sessions. Session A 13:29-14:44 UTC (30K TRITON pair, 30K explicit-FlashInfer MTP, the stale-cache crashes, the superseded image=0-only probes); session B 15:27-15:55 UTC (everything else, including the whole 50K quartet). Fresh VM per session, identical stack.

machine.flashinfer: 0.6.16.post3 (vLLM's requirements/cuda.txt pin; contains flashinfer#3739, the Ampere large-head kernel)
machine.note: 60 layers: 50 sliding (head 256, window 1024) + 10 full attention (head 512). The heterogeneous head dims are why Gemma4Config forces TRITON_ATTN whenever FA4 is unavailable - the routing this matrix is about.

method.serving: text-only: limit_mm_per_prompt zeroes image, video and audio. gemma-4 registers all three, and vLLM 0.28.0 drops the mm-prefix backend requirement only when every registered modality is 0. Without that, FlashInfer is rejected at engine init regardless of routing.
method.measurement: batch 1, greedy, ignore_eos; decode tok/s = (64-8)/(t64-t8) over two generations from one prompt after a warm-up generation. Prefix caching keeps t8 at 0.3-0.7s, so the differencing is decode-dominated.
method.runs: single run per cell - a probe, not a campaign. The three cross-checks below and the ROCm depth series carry the conclusion; treat third-digit differences as noise.
method.cache_discipline: torch_compile_cache cleared before every leg (vllm#50891: the AOT cache key ignores limit_mm_per_prompt; a stale artifact crashes engine init).

timing_raw_s.comment: t8/t64 as printed (0.1s precision); decode_tok_s above is the probe's full-precision computation, which is the authoritative figure.

readings.reading: On the forced default, MTP is a net loss that deepens with context (-28.2% at 30K, -61.1% at 50K), the reporter's '3x or higher at 50K+' seen from its lower edge and the ROCm curve's -70.8% at 32K from the harder-hit hardware. On a healthy backend the same MTP is +35.0% at 30K; the residual -8.7% at 50K is drafter economics, not the pathological drop. Mixed auto-selection (FA2 sliding + FlashInfer full, what vllm#47547 produces) is the fastest configuration measured.

mm_prefix_validation.symptom: ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['partial multimodal token full attention not supported']
mm_prefix_validation.mechanism: multimodal-enabled gemma-4 sets use_mm_prefix=True; validate_configuration excludes every backend without supports_mm_prefix(); FlashInfer never overrides the False default. Fires on explicit selection too. Gate drops only when all three registered modalities are limit-0 (log line: 'running in text-only mode').
mm_prefix_validation.consequence: FlashInfer is structurally unavailable to multimodal-enabled gemma-4 deployments on 0.28.0; vllm#46558 is adding the missing mm-prefix support.

aot_cache_collision_50891.symptom: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size' at dynamo call_size, inside 'Directly load AOT compilation' during profile_run
aot_cache_collision_50891.evidence: identical cache hash for materially different configs: 2a7f2e89a041a9e40e919d094d06fd9bd6ff677d79ee0aff01ee26d4f00c3db2 keyed both (image=0, mm on, auto->TRITON, MTP) and (all-zero, mm off, auto->FA2+FlashInfer, MTP); 2b4077ad3de16dd3c894d407455e82c70cdf76a983da3f3650781906ee0c9c5d the no-spec pair. Session B reproduced the same hashes on a fresh VM and, cold, both configs compile and run - the collision is deterministic, the artifact is what crashes.
aot_cache_collision_50891.already_reported: vllm#50891 (open); fix PR vllm#50908's disabled_mm_modalities hash factor separates both pairs; closed vllm#27283 shows the same call_size signature.
aot_cache_collision_50891.logs: logs/session-a/leg3b-*, leg4b-*, errors-tail-3b-4b.txt, cache-fingerprints.txt; fresh-VM control in logs/session-b/leg3d-*, leg4d-*

sessions_caveat: Sessions A and B are different Colab VMs with the identical software stack. No configuration ran on both, so cross-session variance is unquantified; every ratio quoted above except the two 30K FlashInfer/auto comparisons is computed within one session. The 50K quartet - the headline - is entirely session B.
